Card.description:
The points a run asks, from the core's decisions (to_ask and beside).

A card asks the first step that has points to ask: the points nobody was sure of (open)
and, under ask=always, also the judgement points no rule settled. A card that does not
block, after the drawing, applies the same rule to the form, point and detail steps, and
adds the points an approved default settled (by = default). Every point in points is
asked; open keeps its meaning (nobody was sure), so under ask=always a point can be
asked with open = false. A null answer ("decide for me") keeps the chosen option,
System 1's lean or else the rules' default, and by stays s1 or rules.

WorkspaceRole.description: key_user reviews the registry; always key_user in v1, which has no auth.

info.description: Ask a question of a workspace's warehouse, revise it by prompt, and follow the run live. A thread is one question plus the runs after it: revisions typed by prompt, follow-ups and nearest questions sent from the transcript, and take-backs; each is one run. Runs are asynchronous: creating one answers 202 with its id, and progress arrives on the run's event stream. Within one pass the phases are contiguous (understand, analyse, present); only reconsider, repair and the hole loop go back, e.g. a reconsider loop can start abstract again after validate, with the phase back at understand. Side states (clarify, ask, propose, reconsider, repair, restore) can appear as a stage. A run can go from complete back to queued under the same id (an answer to a beside-the-chart card, a chart switch); a run.status queued after running means a worker restarted it. Every error is a Problem. There is no auth in v1: calls are same-origin and carry no header.
info.title: sightline API

get.description:
Server-sent events. Each frame is `id: <n>`, `event: <type>` and `data: <RunEvent as JSON>`; ids increase per run. The stream opens with a `retry: 3000` line, so a client reconnects after 3 s. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to get only the frames after it (ids are per-run integers from 1, the same counter as RunView.last_event_id); `?last_event_id=` is the fallback when the header is absent, e.g. on the first connect after getRun. A comment line `: ping` comes every 15 s. The stream ends after a terminal run.status (complete, clarify, failed, cancelled, superseded) or after asking.

A complete run tells, in this order: run.status queued, then running; stage.started and stage.finished per stage, with step.started and step.finished inside analyse; restatement right after bind, and again when the text changes; chart after render, the main chart first, then each small chart with its support_id; card, clarify when it applies, result; the terminal run.status. The storyline and supports ride only on the result event and RunView.result, the follow-ups only on RunView: getRun has them after the terminal run.status.

post.description:
Revise the question by prompt, or send a follow-up or a nearest question from the transcript. Post it directly, never /cancel first: a run of this thread still active is superseded (it ends with status superseded). Cancel is cooperative at stage boundaries, so the old run may emit events for up to a minute; clients drop events of runs that are not the thread's active run.

Each run answers an anchor, which is the question or the latest follow-up or nearest question in its chain, plus the revisions typed after that anchor. A typed revision after a follow-up revises the follow-up. Any standalone question sent from the transcript (a follow-up, a nearest question) becomes the new anchor; composer and card-text revisions never do. A take-back re-runs revision n-1 and copies its anchor; taking back a follow-up re-runs the parent's reading.

With follows: follows.run_id must be the thread's latest run, else 409 not_latest. That run must be complete and follow_up_id one of its follow_ups, else 409 not_answerable. Follow-up ids are unique per run and survive a chart pick, but may vanish after a side-card answer re-presents the run, and a vanished id is not_answerable too. message must equal that follow-up's question, else 422 with errors[0] {loc: [body, message], type: follow_up_mismatch}. A clarify run has no answer, so its nearest questions go with via nearest and no follows.

delete.description: Take back revision n (n >= 1 is the thread's nth run after the question). Like reviseThread, it supersedes a run of this thread still active and starts a new run (origin take_back, takes_back n), whose prompt is the text taken back. It re-runs revision n-1 with that revision's anchor; taking back a follow-up re-runs the parent's reading.
